_regions.bahamas: Bahamas (Bimini, Abaco, Nassau/Berry Islands/Eleuthera). Gulf Stream and Tongue of the Ocean pelagics; spring billfish run.
_regions.cuba: Cuba north coast (Havana–Varadero) and Jardines de la Reina. Summer blue marlin on the north coast; flats/tarpon in the south.
_regions.carib-west: Western Caribbean islands: Cayman Islands and Jamaica. Spring and autumn blue marlin, winter wahoo/dolphin.
_regions.carib-east: Mona Passage and Virgin Islands: eastern Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico, USVI, BVI. Summer blue marlin (North Drop Aug), spring white marlin (Cap Cana Apr–May), winter dolphin/wahoo/sailfish.

_sources._all: LOW confidence overall: built from tournament calendars, charter/fishing-press reports and general knowledge; no published monthly catch-rate data were found for these islands. Tune with captains' reports.
_sources.blue-marlin: Bahamas: bluewater season Mar–early Jul (Sport Fishing Mag, Bimini: https://www.sportfishingmag.com/story/travel/bimini-the-original-island-in-the-stream/). Cuba: Hemingway tournament held May/June (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_Hemingway_International_Billfishing_Tournament), north-coast peak Aug–Sep (low). Jamaica: Port Antonio International Marlin Tournament Sep/Oct (Jamaica Gleaner 2024/2025, e.g. https://web4.jamaica-gleaner.com/article/sports/20240914/all-set-september-23-28-port-antonio-international-marlin-tournament). East: Cap Cana peak Jun–Aug, Casa de Campo Feb–Apr (Marlin Mag https://www.marlinmag.com/travel/marlin-fishing-in-dominican-republic-cap-cana-casa-de-campo/); USVI North Drop: big tournaments on the July and August full moons (https://virginislandsthisweek.com/st-thomas/st-thomas-water-activities/summer-sportfishing-season/); San Juan International Billfish Tournament late Aug/Sep (low).
_sources.white-marlin: Cap Cana: Mar–Jun, best Apr–May (Marlin Mag, above). Bahamas spring (low). Rare in Cayman/Jamaica (low).
_sources.pacific-sailfish: Atlantic sailfish (the app uses one key for both oceans). DR: Jan–Feb excellent (Marlin Mag). Bahamas/Cuba: winter along the Gulf Stream/Straits (low).
_sources.swordfish: Deep-drop daytime fishery exists (Bahamas, Cuba, PR) but little documented — flat 1 (low).
_sources.yellowfin-tuna: Bahamas spring run May–Jun (Bimini/Cat Cay, low); Cayman spring and Jamaica winter (low).
_sources.dorado: Winter–spring peak Jan–May across the region (PR/USVI/DR charter reports; low).
_sources.wahoo: Bimini: Nov–Mar run (Sport Fishing Mag). Same winter peak used elsewhere (low).
_sources.tarpon: Jardines de la Reina: spring–summer (low). San Juan lagoons year-round (low).
_sources.bonefish: Bahamas flats year-round (Sport Fishing Mag, Bimini); spring/fall peaks (low).
_sources.mutton-snapper: Seasons are availability only; closures are applied separately (USVI Apr–Jun, PR Apr–May territorial / Apr–Jun federal).
_sources.black-grouper: Availability only; USVI closure Feb–Apr applied separately; PR closure is federal-only (see rules.json limits).
_sources.cobia: Listed by the Bahamas Ministry of Tourism as a flats species; occasional elsewhere (low).
_sources.bull-shark: Bahamas: all shark fishing banned — closure in rules.json zeroes it there.
_sources.shortfin-mako: null: retention prohibited in US Caribbean waters (NOAA HMS 2026), sharks fully protected in The Bahamas, ICCAT North Atlantic non-retention; rare in these warm surface waters. Recommend not mapping here.
_sources.blue-shark: null: rare in warm Caribbean surface waters; not a sport target here.
_sources.spanish-mackerel: null: S. maculatus is a US/Gulf species; island "sierras" here are cero and king mackerel.
_sources.red-drum: null: not found in the islands.
_sources.red-snapper: null: Lutjanus campechanus is a Gulf/US species; the islands' "red snappers" are other species (silk, blackfin).
_sources.yellowtail-snapper: New species. Year-round reef staple; spring–summer spawning peaks (SEDAR 64; FishBase). Bahamas has a designated yellowtail snapper spawning site (Steven's Rock).
